records.source: Καὶ ἐδόθη μοι κάλαμος ὅμοιος ῥάβδῳ, λέγων· Ἔγειρε καὶ μέτρησον τὸν ναὸν τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ τὸ θυσιαστήριον καὶ τοὺς προσκυνοῦντας ἐν αὐτῷ.
records.gloss: And was given to me a reed like to a staff, saying: Rise and measure the temple of the God and the altar and those worshiping in it.
pieces: I was given a measuring rod like a staff and told, "Get up and measure God's temple and the altar, and count those who worship there.

L.1: And a reed like a staff was given to me, [someone] saying, "Rise and measure the temple of God and the altar and those who worship in it.

R.1: Then I was given a stick for measuring, like a long rod. I was told, "Get up and measure God's temple and the altar. Count the people who worship there.

decisions.choice: measuring: marking out what God protects
decisions.reason: Ezekiel watched a man with a measuring reed measure the new temple (Ezekiel 40-42), and Zechariah saw a man measure Jerusalem, which God would guard as a wall of fire (Zechariah 2:1-5). To measure the temple and its worshipers is to mark them out as God's own and under his protection.

decisions.choice: the temple and its worshipers: God's people
decisions.reason: Revelation was most likely written after the temple in Jerusalem was destroyed in AD 70, and elsewhere in the New Testament God's people are his temple (1 Corinthians 3:16; Ephesians 2:21; compare Revelation 3:12). Many therefore take the measured temple as the people of God, kept safe in their worship while the outer court is trampled. Others take it as a literal temple. The text uses the language of the Jerusalem temple and does not explain it.

decisions.choice: saying: the speaker is not named
decisions.reason: λέγων "saying" has no subject. The voice speaks of "my two witnesses" (11:3), so it is God's or Christ's, perhaps through the angel of chapter 10. The speech runs to the end of 11:3.

decisions.choice: count those who worship (B, R)
decisions.reason: One does not measure people with a rod; Balanced and Readable say "count", which is what measuring them means.

records.heading: The two witnesses

records.source: καὶ τὴν αὐλὴν τὴν ἔξωθεν τοῦ ναοῦ ἔκβαλε ἔξωθεν, καὶ μὴ αὐτὴν μετρήσῃς, ὅτι ἐδόθη τοῖς ἔθνεσιν, καὶ τὴν πόλιν τὴν ἁγίαν πατήσουσιν μῆνας τεσσεράκοντα δύο.
records.gloss: And the courtyard the outside of the temple throw out outside and not it measure, because it was given to the nations, and the city the holy they will trample months forty-two.
pieces: But leave out the court outside the temple; do not measure it, for it has been handed over to the nations, and they will tread the holy city underfoot for forty-two months.

L.2: And leave out the court that is outside the temple, and do not measure it, because it has been given to the nations, and they will trample the holy city forty-two months.

R.2: But do not measure the courtyard outside the temple. Leave it out. It has been given to the nations who do not know God. They will trample on the holy city for forty-two months.

decisions.choice: forty-two months: the limited time of trial
decisions.reason: Forty-two months is three and a half years, the same as 1,260 days (11:3; 12:6) and "a time, times and half a time" (12:14). It comes from Daniel, where a power persecutes the saints for that time (Daniel 7:25; 12:7). It is a limited time of suffering, set by God, and recurs in 13:5.

decisions.choice: the holy city trampled by the nations: Jesus's words
decisions.reason: Jesus said that Jerusalem would be trampled by the nations until the times of the nations are fulfilled (Luke 21:24). ἔθνεσιν means the nations, those outside God's people.

decisions.choice: the nations who do not know God (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says that the nations here are those outside God's people (m2).

records.source: καὶ δώσω τοῖς δυσὶν μάρτυσίν μου, καὶ προφητεύσουσιν ἡμέρας χιλίας διακοσίας ἑξήκοντα, περιβεβλημένοι σάκκους.
records.gloss: And I will give to the two witnesses of me, and they will prophesy days 1,260, having been clothed in sackcloths.
pieces: I will give power to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} two witnesses, and they will prophesy for 1,260 days, dressed in sackcloth."

L.3: And I will grant [authority] to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} two witnesses, and they will prophesy 1,260 days, clothed in sackcloth."

R.3: I will send {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} two witnesses. They will speak God's message for 1,260 days. They will wear rough clothes to show sorrow."

decisions.choice: the two witnesses: who they are
alternatives: two individual prophets of the end, like Moses and Elijah
the witnessing church, pictured as two prophets
decisions.reason: Their powers are those of Elijah, who shut the sky, and Moses, who turned water to blood (11:6). But they are also called two lampstands (11:4), and the lampstands in Revelation are churches (1:20). Two witnesses were needed for testimony to stand (Deuteronomy 19:15). Many therefore read them as a picture of the church in its prophetic witness; others as two individuals. The text does not settle it.

decisions.choice: sackcloth: the clothing of mourning and repentance
decisions.reason: See the note on 6:12. Prophets wore it when calling people to repent (Jonah 3:5-8; compare Isaiah 20:2).

decisions.choice: I will give: the object is understood
decisions.reason: δώσω has no object. The sense is that God grants the witnesses power, or appoints them, to prophesy.

decisions.choice: [authority] (L); power (B); send (R)
decisions.reason: Every level supplies what the bare "I will give" implies (m3).

decisions.choice: my: deity pronoun setting
decisions.reason: The speaker is God or Christ, so "my" takes the deity pronoun setting.

records.source: Οὗτοί εἰσιν αἱ δύο ἐλαῖαι καὶ αἱ δύο λυχνίαι αἱ ἐνώπιον τοῦ κυρίου τῆς γῆς ἑστῶτες.
records.gloss: These are the two olive trees and the two lampstands the [ones] before the Lord of the earth standing.
pieces: These two are the olive trees and the lampstands that stand before the Lord of the earth.

L.4: These are the two olive trees and the two lampstands that stand before the Lord of the earth.

R.4: These two witnesses are the two olive trees and the two lampstands that stand in front of the Lord of the whole earth.

decisions.choice: two olive trees and lampstands: Zechariah 4
decisions.reason: Zechariah saw a lampstand with two olive trees beside it, and was told that they are "the two anointed ones who stand by the Lord of the whole earth" (Zechariah 4:2-3, 11-14), Zerubbabel the governor and Joshua the priest. The witnesses carry on that role, kept supplied by God's Spirit (Zechariah 4:6).

records.source: καὶ εἴ τις αὐτοὺς θέλει ἀδικῆσαι, πῦρ ἐκπορεύεται ἐκ τοῦ στόματος αὐτῶν καὶ κατεσθίει τοὺς ἐχθροὺς αὐτῶν· καὶ εἴ τις θελήσῃ αὐτοὺς ἀδικῆσαι, οὕτως δεῖ αὐτὸν ἀποκτανθῆναι.
records.gloss: And if anyone them wishes to harm, fire comes out out of the mouth of them and devours the enemies of them; and if anyone should wish them to harm, thus it is necessary him to be killed.
pieces: Should anyone want to hurt them, fire comes out of their mouths and burns up their enemies. Whoever wants to hurt them is bound to be killed like this.

L.5: And if anyone wants to harm them, fire comes out of their mouth and devours their enemies; and if anyone wants to harm them, in this way {{gender:that person|he}} must be killed.

R.5: If anyone tries to hurt them, fire comes out of their mouths and destroys their enemies. That is how anyone who tries to hurt them will die.

decisions.choice: fire from their mouth: Elijah and Jeremiah
decisions.reason: Elijah called down fire on those sent to seize him (2 Kings 1:10-12). God told Jeremiah, "I am making my words in your mouth a fire, and this people wood, and it shall consume them" (Jeremiah 5:14). The fire coming from their mouths suggests the power of their word.

decisions.choice: protected until their work is done
decisions.reason: No one can harm the witnesses while they bear their testimony. Only when they have finished does the beast kill them (11:7).

records.source: οὗτοι ἔχουσιν τὴν ἐξουσίαν κλεῖσαι τὸν οὐρανόν, ἵνα μὴ ὑετὸς βρέχῃ τὰς ἡμέρας τῆς προφητείας αὐτῶν, καὶ ἐξουσίαν ἔχουσιν ἐπὶ τῶν ὑδάτων στρέφειν αὐτὰ εἰς αἷμα καὶ πατάξαι τὴν γῆν ἐν πάσῃ πληγῇ ὁσάκις ἐὰν θελήσωσιν.
records.gloss: These have the authority to shut the sky, so that not rain falls the days of the prophecy of them, and authority they have over the waters to turn them into blood and to strike the earth with every plague as often as they wish.
pieces: It is in their power to close the sky, so that no rain falls in the days of their prophecy; they also have power over the waters, to turn them into blood, and power to strike the earth with every kind of plague whenever they choose.

L.6: These have the power to shut the sky, so that no rain falls during the days of their prophecy, and they have power over the waters to turn them into blood and to strike the earth with every plague as often as they wish.

R.6: They have power to stop the rain from falling while they are speaking God's message. They have power to turn water into blood. They can send any kind of plague on the earth as often as they want.

decisions.choice: shutting the sky: Elijah
decisions.reason: Elijah told King Ahab that there would be no rain except at his word (1 Kings 17:1), and the drought lasted three and a half years (Luke 4:25; James 5:17), the same length as the witnesses' prophecy.

decisions.choice: water to blood and plagues: Moses
decisions.reason: Moses turned the Nile to blood and struck Egypt with plagues (Exodus 7-11).

records.source: Καὶ ὅταν τελέσωσιν τὴν μαρτυρίαν αὐτῶν, τὸ θηρίον τὸ ἀναβαῖνον ἐκ τῆς ἀβύσσου ποιήσει μετ’ αὐτῶν πόλεμον καὶ νικήσει αὐτοὺς καὶ ἀποκτενεῖ αὐτούς.
records.gloss: And when they finish the testimony of them, the beast the [one] coming up out of the abyss will make with them war and will overcome them and will kill them.
pieces: When they have completed their testimony, the beast that rises from the abyss will wage war against them, overpower them, and kill them.

L.7: And when they have finished their testimony, the beast that comes up out of the abyss will make war with them and overcome them and kill them.

R.7: When they have finished telling God's message, the beast that comes up out of the bottomless pit will fight against them. It will defeat them and kill them.

decisions.choice: the beast makes war and prevails: Daniel 7:21
decisions.reason: Daniel saw a horn that made war with the saints and prevailed over them until the Ancient of Days came (Daniel 7:21-22). This is the first mention of "the beast" in Revelation; it is described in chapters 13 and 17. It comes up from the abyss (9:1-2; 17:8).

decisions.choice: overcome: the beast's apparent victory
decisions.reason: νικήσει is the verb used of the victory of Christ and his people (3:21; 5:5). The beast seems to win, but the witnesses rise (11:11), and the faithful overcome by their testimony even to death (12:11).

decisions.choice: overcome (L); overpower (B); defeat (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the word of the letters so the link can be seen (m2); Balanced and Readable use words for victory in battle.

records.source: καὶ τὸ πτῶμα αὐτῶν ἐπὶ τῆς πλατείας τῆς πόλεως τῆς μεγάλης, ἥτις καλεῖται πνευματικῶς Σόδομα καὶ Αἴγυπτος, ὅπου καὶ ὁ κύριος αὐτῶν ἐσταυρώθη.
records.gloss: And the corpse of them on the street of the city the great, which is called spiritually Sodom and Egypt, where also the Lord of them was crucified.
pieces: Their bodies will lie in the open street of the great city, which in a prophetic sense is called Sodom and Egypt, where their Lord too was crucified.

L.8: And their corpse [will lie] in the street of the great city, which is spiritually called Sodom and Egypt, where also their Lord was crucified.

R.8: Their dead bodies will lie in the street of the great city. That city is like Sodom and Egypt, places that were wicked and fought against God. It is also the city where their Lord was nailed to a cross.

decisions.choice: the great city: which city is meant
alternatives: Jerusalem, where the Lord was crucified
Rome or Babylon, the "great city" of 16:19 and 17:18
the world's city, opposed to God, in every age
decisions.reason: "Where their Lord was crucified" points to Jerusalem. But elsewhere in Revelation "the great city" is Babylon (16:19; 17:18; 18:10), and here the city is named "spiritually" Sodom and Egypt, places of wickedness and of the oppression of God's people. Many therefore take it as the city of this world in its hostility to God, which crucified the Lord and kills his witnesses.

decisions.choice: spiritually: in the Spirit's way of speaking, as a prophetic name
decisions.reason: πνευματικῶς means "spiritually" or "by the Spirit". The names Sodom and Egypt are not geography but the Spirit's judgment on what the city is like (compare Isaiah 1:10, where Jerusalem's rulers are called rulers of Sodom).

decisions.choice: corpse: one word for both bodies
decisions.reason: πτῶμα is singular, used for both, as in 11:9 before the plural.

decisions.choice: places that were wicked and fought against God (R)
decisions.reason: Readable explains why the city is given these names (m2).

records.source: καὶ βλέπουσιν ἐκ τῶν λαῶν καὶ φυλῶν καὶ γλωσσῶν καὶ ἐθνῶν τὸ πτῶμα αὐτῶν ἡμέρας τρεῖς καὶ ἥμισυ, καὶ τὰ πτώματα αὐτῶν οὐκ ἀφίουσιν τεθῆναι εἰς μνῆμα.
records.gloss: And see [some] out of the peoples and tribes and tongues and nations the corpse of them days three and a half, and the corpses of them not they allow to be placed into a tomb.
pieces: People from among the peoples, tribes, languages, and nations look on their bodies for three and a half days and will not let them be laid in a tomb.

L.9: And [some] from the peoples and tribes and languages and nations look at their corpse for three and a half days, and they do not allow their corpses to be placed in a tomb.

R.9: For three and a half days, people from every nation, tribe, language, and people will look at their dead bodies. They will not let anyone bury them.

decisions.choice: refusing burial: the greatest dishonor
decisions.reason: To leave the dead unburied was a terrible disgrace (Psalm 79:2-3; Jeremiah 8:1-2). The world puts the witnesses' bodies on display.

decisions.choice: three and a half days: a short time, matching the three and a half years
decisions.reason: The witnesses prophesy for three and a half years and lie dead for three and a half days: the triumph of their enemies is brief.

records.source: καὶ οἱ κατοικοῦντες ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς χαίρουσιν ἐπ’ αὐτοῖς καὶ εὐφραίνονται, καὶ δῶρα πέμψουσιν ἀλλήλοις, ὅτι οὗτοι οἱ δύο προφῆται ἐβασάνισαν τοὺς κατοικοῦντας ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς.
records.gloss: And those dwelling on the earth rejoice over them and celebrate, and gifts they will send to one another, because these the two prophets tormented those dwelling on the earth.
pieces: Those who live on the earth rejoice over their death and make merry; they will exchange gifts, because these two prophets had tormented the people of the earth.

L.10: And those who live on the earth rejoice over them and celebrate, and they will send gifts to one another, because these two prophets tormented those who live on the earth.

R.10: The people on earth will be happy that the two witnesses are dead. They will have parties and give each other presents. They are glad because these two prophets made them suffer.

decisions.choice: sending gifts: a festival of celebration
decisions.reason: Sending gifts to one another was a way of keeping a festival, as the Jews did at Purim when they were rescued from their enemies (Esther 9:19, 22). Here the world celebrates the death of God's prophets.

decisions.choice: tormented: by the plagues, and by their message
decisions.reason: The witnesses struck the earth with plagues (11:6), and their call to repent troubled the consciences of those who refused it.

records.source: Καὶ μετὰ τὰς τρεῖς ἡμέρας καὶ ἥμισυ πνεῦμα ζωῆς ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ εἰσῆλθεν ἐν αὐτοῖς, καὶ ἔστησαν ἐπὶ τοὺς πόδας αὐτῶν, καὶ φόβος μέγας ἐπέπεσεν ἐπὶ τοὺς θεωροῦντας αὐτούς·
records.gloss: And after the three days and half, spirit of life out of the God entered into them, and they stood on the feet of them, and fear great fell on those seeing them.
pieces: After the three and a half days, though, the breath of life came into them from God; they rose to their feet, and those watching were seized by great fear.

L.11: And after the three and a half days, the breath of life from God entered into them, and they stood on their feet, and great fear fell on those who saw them.

R.11: But after three and a half days, God breathed life into them again. They stood up, and the people who saw them were terrified.

decisions.choice: the breath of life: Ezekiel's valley of dry bones
decisions.reason: In Ezekiel 37:5, 10 God's breath enters the dry bones, and they live and stand on their feet, a great army. πνεῦμα means breath, wind or spirit, as the Hebrew word in Ezekiel does.

decisions.choice: breath (L, B); breathed (R)
decisions.reason: "Breath" keeps the link with Ezekiel 37 and with God breathing life into the first man (Genesis 2:7).

records.source: καὶ ἤκουσαν φωνῆς μεγάλης ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ λεγούσης αὐτοῖς· Ἀνάβατε ὧδε, καὶ ἀνέβησαν εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν ἐν τῇ νεφέλῃ, καὶ ἐθεώρησαν αὐτοὺς οἱ ἐχθροὶ αὐτῶν.
records.gloss: And they heard a voice great out of the heaven saying to them: Come up here. And they went up into the heaven in the cloud, and saw them the enemies of them.
pieces: A great voice from heaven called to them, "Come up here!" They heard it, and up they went into heaven in the cloud, with their enemies watching them.

L.12: And they heard a loud voice from heaven saying to them, "Come up here!" And they went up into heaven in the cloud, and their enemies watched them.

R.12: Then the two witnesses heard a loud voice from heaven. It said, "Come up here!" So they went up to heaven in a cloud while their enemies watched.

decisions.choice: they heard
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads "they heard". Some manuscripts read "I heard". The translation follows the SBLGNT. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: taken up in a cloud: Elijah and Jesus
decisions.reason: Elijah was taken up to heaven (2 Kings 2:11), and Jesus was taken up in a cloud as his followers watched (Acts 1:9). The witnesses share their Lord's death, resurrection and ascension, and their enemies see it.

records.source: καὶ ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ὥρᾳ ἐγένετο σεισμὸς μέγας, καὶ τὸ δέκατον τῆς πόλεως ἔπεσεν, καὶ ἀπεκτάνθησαν ἐν τῷ σεισμῷ ὀνόματα ἀνθρώπων χιλιάδες ἑπτά, καὶ οἱ λοιποὶ ἔμφοβοι ἐγένοντο καὶ ἔδωκαν δόξαν τῷ θεῷ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ.
records.gloss: And in that the hour there was earthquake great, and the tenth of the city fell, and were killed in the earthquake names of men thousands seven, and the rest terrified became and gave glory to the God of the heaven.
pieces: In that same hour a great earthquake struck, a tenth of the city fell, and the quake killed 7,000 {{gender:people|men}}. The rest were filled with fear and gave glory to the God of heaven.

L.13: And in that hour there was a great earthquake, and a tenth of the city fell, and 7,000 names of {{gender:people|men}} were killed in the earthquake, and the rest became terrified and gave glory to the God of heaven.

R.13: At that moment there was a powerful earthquake. A tenth of the city fell down. The earthquake killed 7,000 {{gender:people|men}}. Everyone else was terrified, and they gave glory to the God of heaven.

decisions.choice: gave glory to God: they turned to God in fear
decisions.reason: To give glory to God is to acknowledge him, the response the angel calls for in 14:7 and that the people refuse in 16:9. After the plagues, which brought no repentance (9:20-21), the witness of the two prophets brings many to fear God. Whether this is full repentance the text does not say.

decisions.choice: a tenth and 7,000: most are spared
decisions.reason: Only a tenth of the city falls. In Elijah's day God kept 7,000 who had not bowed to Baal (1 Kings 19:18); here 7,000 die and the rest, the great majority, give glory to God. ὀνόματα, "names", means persons, as in 3:4.

decisions.choice: people | men
decisions.reason: The word includes men and women.

records.source: Ἡ οὐαὶ ἡ δευτέρα ἀπῆλθεν· ἰδοὺ ἡ οὐαὶ ἡ τρίτη ἔρχεται ταχύ.
records.gloss: The woe the second has passed; behold the woe the third comes quickly.
pieces: The second woe is over. Look: the third woe is coming soon.

L.14: The second woe has passed; look, the third woe is coming soon.

R.14: The second terrible thing is over. The third is coming soon.

decisions.choice: the second woe ends; the third is the seventh trumpet
decisions.reason: The second woe began with the sixth trumpet (9:13) and has included the scroll and the witnesses. The third comes with the seventh trumpet, whose judgments unfold in the chapters that follow.

decisions.choice: woe (L, B); terrible thing (R)
decisions.reason: As in 8:13.

records.source: Καὶ ὁ ἕβδομος ἄγγελος ἐσάλπισεν· καὶ ἐγένοντο φωναὶ μεγάλαι ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ λέγοντες· Ἐγένετο ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ κόσμου τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν καὶ τοῦ χριστοῦ αὐτοῦ, καὶ βασιλεύσει εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων.
records.gloss: And the seventh angel blew trumpet, and there were voices great in the heaven saying: Has become the kingdom of the world of the Lord of us and of the Christ of him, and he will reign into the ages of the ages.
pieces: Then the seventh angel blew his trumpet, and loud voices in heaven said: "The rule over the world now belongs to our Lord and to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will reign forever and ever."

L.15: And the seventh angel blew his trumpet, and there were loud voices in heaven, saying, "The kingdom of the world has become [the kingdom] of our Lord and of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will reign for the ages of the ages."

R.15: The seventh angel blew his trumpet. Then loud voices in heaven said, "Now our Lord and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} rule over the world! He will rule forever and ever!"

decisions.choice: the kingdom of our Lord and his Anointed: Psalm 2 and Daniel
decisions.reason: Psalm 2:2 speaks of the nations raging "against the LORD and against his Anointed"; χριστοῦ is the Greek for "anointed". Daniel foretells a kingdom that God will set up and that will stand forever (Daniel 2:44; 7:14, 27). Now the rule of the world has passed to God and his Messiah.

decisions.choice: has become: announced as already done
decisions.reason: Ἐγένετο is past: the heavenly voices speak of God's kingdom as already come. This is the completion of "the mystery of God" promised in 10:7.

decisions.choice: he will reign: one reign of God and his Christ
decisions.reason: After naming both "our Lord and his Christ", the verb is singular: "he will reign". The reign of God and of Christ is one (compare 22:3, "the throne of God and of the Lamb").

decisions.choice: the kingdom of the world: rule over the world
decisions.reason: βασιλεία means royal rule or a realm. "The kingdom of the world" is the rule over it that the powers of the world have claimed.

decisions.choice: his Christ | his Messiah
decisions.reason: With "his", every level writes the christos setting without "the" in the alternative.

records.heading: The seventh trumpet

records.source: Καὶ οἱ εἴκοσι τέσσαρες πρεσβύτεροι οἱ ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ καθήμενοι ἐπὶ τοὺς θρόνους αὐτῶν ἔπεσαν ἐπὶ τὰ πρόσωπα αὐτῶν καὶ προσεκύνησαν τῷ θεῷ, λέγοντες· Εὐχαριστοῦμέν σοι, κύριε, ὁ θεός, ὁ παντοκράτωρ, ὁ ὢν καὶ ὁ ἦν, ὅτι εἴληφας τὴν δύναμίν σου τὴν μεγάλην καὶ ἐβασίλευσας.
records.gloss: And the twenty-four elders the before the God sitting on the thrones of them fell on the faces of them and worshiped the God, \v 17 saying: We give thanks to you, Lord the God the Almighty, the [one] being and the [one who] was, because you have taken the power of you the great and began to reign.
pieces: Then the twenty-four elders who sit on their thrones in God's presence threw themselves face down and worshiped God.

"Lord God, the Almighty," they said, "the one who is and who was, we thank {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have taken {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} great power into {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hands and begun {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} reign.

L.16: And the twenty-four elders who sit on their thrones before God fell on their faces and worshiped God,
L.17: saying, "We give thanks to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, Lord God the Almighty, who is and who was, because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have taken {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} great power and have begun to reign.

R.16: The twenty-four elders were sitting on their thrones in front of God. They bowed down with their faces to the ground and worshiped God.
R.17: They said, "Lord God, the Almighty, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} always were. We thank {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have used {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} great power and have begun to rule as king.

decisions.choice: who is and who was: no longer "who is coming"
decisions.reason: In 1:4, 8 and 4:8 God is the one "who is and who was and who is coming". Here the last part is gone: he has come, and his reign has begun. The same shortened title appears in 16:5.

decisions.choice: you have begun to reign
decisions.reason: ἐβασίλευσας is past, and here it means entering on a reign: God has taken up his kingly rule openly.

decisions.choice: you, your: deity pronoun setting
decisions.reason: The elders speak to God.

records.source: καὶ τὰ ἔθνη ὠργίσθησαν, καὶ ἦλθεν ἡ ὀργή σου καὶ ὁ καιρὸς τῶν νεκρῶν κριθῆναι καὶ δοῦναι τὸν μισθὸν τοῖς δούλοις σου τοῖς προφήταις καὶ τοῖς ἁγίοις καὶ τοῖς φοβουμένοις τὸ ὄνομά σου, τοὺς μικροὺς καὶ τοὺς μεγάλους, καὶ διαφθεῖραι τοὺς διαφθείροντας τὴν γῆν.
records.gloss: And the nations were angry, and came the wrath of you and the time of the dead to be judged and to give the reward to the slaves of you the prophets and to the saints and to those fearing the name of you, the small and the great, and to destroy those destroying the earth.
pieces: The nations raged, but {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} wrath has come, and the time for the dead to be judged, for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servants the prophets to be rewarded, and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} holy people, and all who fear {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name, small and great, and the time to destroy those who destroy the earth."

L.18: And the nations were enraged, and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} wrath came, and the time for the dead to be judged, and to give the reward to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} slaves the prophets and to the saints and to those who fear {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name, the small and the great, and to destroy those who destroy the earth."

R.18: The nations were angry, but now it is time for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to show {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} anger. It is time to judge the dead. It is time to reward {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servants the prophets, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} holy people, and everyone who honors {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name, whether they are important or not. It is time to destroy those who are destroying the earth."

decisions.choice: the nations raged: Psalm 2
decisions.reason: "Why do the nations rage?" (Psalm 2:1), and God speaks to them in his wrath (Psalm 2:5). ὠργίσθησαν and ὀργή are the same root: the nations' anger is met by God's.

decisions.choice: destroying the destroyers of the earth
decisions.reason: διαφθεῖραι and διαφθείροντας are the same verb, which means both to destroy and to corrupt. Those who ruin God's creation are themselves ruined. The Greek of Genesis 6:11-13 uses the same word of the earth corrupted before the flood.

decisions.choice: the small and the great: everyone
decisions.reason: The phrase means all people regardless of rank (Psalm 115:13; Revelation 13:16; 19:5; 20:12). The Greek changes case here, as if starting a new list.

decisions.choice: saints (L); your holy people (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 5:8.

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it (1:1); Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: Καὶ ἠνοίγη ὁ ναὸς τοῦ θεοῦ ὁ ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ, καὶ ὤφθη ἡ κιβωτὸς τῆς διαθήκης αὐτοῦ ἐν τῷ ναῷ αὐτοῦ· καὶ ἐγένοντο ἀστραπαὶ καὶ φωναὶ καὶ βρονταὶ καὶ σεισμὸς καὶ χάλαζα μεγάλη.
records.gloss: And was opened the temple of the God the in the heaven, and was seen the ark of the covenant of him in the temple of him, and there were lightnings and voices and thunders and earthquake and hail great.
pieces: God's temple in heaven was thrown open, and inside it the ark of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} covenant appeared. Lightning flashed; there were loud sounds and thunder, an earthquake, and huge hail.

L.19: And the temple of God in heaven was opened, and the ark of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} covenant was seen in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} temple, and there were lightnings and voices and thunders and an earthquake and great hail.

R.19: Then God's temple in heaven was opened. Inside the temple people could see the ark of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} covenant, the sacred box of God's promises. There was lightning, loud noise, thunder, an earthquake, and a terrible hailstorm.

decisions.choice: the ark of the covenant: the sign of God's presence and promise
decisions.reason: The ark was the gold-covered chest in the inner room of the tabernacle and temple, holding the tablets of the covenant (Exodus 25:10-22). It was lost when Babylon destroyed the temple in 587 BC, and Jeremiah 3:16 says it would not be remade. Now it is seen in heaven: God has kept his covenant.

decisions.choice: the signs of God's presence, now with hail
decisions.reason: The lightning, sounds and thunder of 4:5 and 8:5, with the earthquake and now great hail, mark the coming of God in judgment (16:18-21).

decisions.choice: the sacred box of God's promises (R)
decisions.reason: Readable explains what the ark was (m1).
